Build the CTest input table from interpreted cycle wavelengths

Source: R/ctest_input.R
ctest_input.Rd

Build the CTest input table from interpreted cycle wavelengths

Usage

ctest_input(
  age,
  e405,
  e125,
  e95,
  obl = c(NA, NA),
  p1 = c(NA, NA),
  p2 = c(NA, NA),
  p3 = c(NA, NA)
)

Arguments

age

Age range of the record in Ma (numeric vector c(min, max)); the secular frequencies are sampled within it in ctest. Required, no default.

e405, e125, e95

Wavelength ranges of the 405-kyr, ~125-kyr and ~95-kyr eccentricity cycles in the depth-domain spectrum, in metres (numeric vectors c(min, max); the order of the two values does not matter). Required, no default.

obl

Wavelength range of the obliquity cycle (k+s3), in metres (numeric vector c(min, max)); c(NA, NA) when no obliquity is interpreted (then use mode="P" in ctest). Default=c(NA, NA).

p1, p2, p3

Wavelength ranges of the precession cycles, in metres (numeric vectors c(min, max)), in the row order of the published spreadsheet, i.e. by decreasing period: p1 the longest (k+g5, ~23.7 kyr today), p2 k+g2 (~22.4 kyr), p3 the shortest (k+g4 and k+g3 together, ~19 kyr); c(NA, NA) when not interpreted (then use mode="T" in ctest). Note: the comments inside the published functions label these rows the other way round, but the code tests them in the order used here (row 6 against k+g5, row 7 against k+g2, row 8 against k+g4 and k+g3). Default=c(NA, NA) for each.

Value

the 8x2 matrix used by ctest(), in the published layout (column 1 = lower frequency = longer wavelength)
